title: Kuku Kohli, Director Who Launched Ajay Devgn in Phool Aur Kaante, Dies at 77
excerpt: The veteran Bollywood filmmaker, whose 1991 debut gave Hindi cinema one of its most iconic opening sequences, died of cardiac arrest at Mumbai's Kokilaben Hospital.
body:
• Kuku Kohli died on August 25 at Kokilaben Hospital in Mumbai after suffering a massive heart attack at age 77
  • His 1991 directorial debut Phool Aur Kaante launched Ajay Devgn's career with the iconic motorcycle-split sequence
  • Kohli directed several commercially successful films through the 1990s and is survived by his wife, actress Aruna Irani

Veteran Bollywood director Kuku Kohli, who gave Ajay Devgn his breakthrough role in the 1991 hit Phool Aur Kaante, died on Tuesday, August 25, at Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital in Mumbai after suffering a massive heart attack. He was 77.

Born Sandesh Kohli, the filmmaker had been admitted to the hospital a few days earlier after feeling unwell. He underwent a procedure to have a stent fitted on Monday, and appeared to be recovering before his condition suddenly deteriorated on Tuesday evening. His brother-in-law, actor Balraj Irani, confirmed the news.

"He was absolutely fine and then today evening he suffered a massive heart attack. He was talking to us and just collapsed," Irani told India Today.

The Film That Changed Bollywood

Kohli's directorial debut, Phool Aur Kaante (1991), became one of the defining films of 1990s Hindi cinema. The action drama introduced Ajay Devgn as a leading man and featured what became one of Bollywood's most iconic debut sequences — Devgn performing a split while balancing between two moving motorcycles. The image endures as a cultural reference point in Indian cinema more than three decades later.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=DOAmVbK3Pzo

The film, which also starred Madhoo Shah, Amrish Puri, Aruna Irani, and Jagdeep, was a commercial success and established Kohli as a filmmaker capable of delivering mass-market entertainment.

"Some people change the course of your life forever. Kuku ji was one of those people for me. Forever grateful for the faith you had in me. You will be deeply missed, Kuku ji. Om Shanti."

— Ajay Devgn, via X (Twitter)

A Career Spanning 1990s Bollywood

Following Phool Aur Kaante, Kohli directed a string of films that defined the decade's commercial cinema. Suhaag (1994), starring Ajay Devgn alongside Akshay Kumar, Karisma Kapoor, and Nagma, was a hit that marked the first on-screen pairing of Devgn and Kumar. He followed with Haqeeqat (1995), featuring Devgn and Tabu, and went on to direct Zulmi (1999), Anari No. 1 (1999), and Yeh Dil Aashiqanaa (2002). His last directorial venture, Woh Tera Naam Tha, was released in 2004.

His films were widely recognized for their emotional storytelling, chart-topping music, and broad mainstream appeal — hallmarks of a period when music-driven romantic dramas and action entertainers dominated the Hindi box office.

Industry Mourns a Mentor

The Indian Motion Picture Producers' Association (IMPPA) President Abhay Sinha described the loss as "sad and shocking." Producer-director Ashoke Pandit shared a throwback photograph with Kohli on Instagram, writing, "Will miss you Kuku ji. Om Shanti."

Madhoo Shah, who starred opposite Devgn in Phool Aur Kaante, mourned Kohli's death on her Instagram. Several other film personalities gathered at his funeral, held at the Oshiwara crematorium in Mumbai, to pay their final respects.

Personal Life

Kohli married actress Aruna Irani in 1990. He is survived by Irani and two daughters, Pooja and Karishma, from his first marriage to Rita Kohli. Aruna Irani, who appeared in Phool Aur Kaante and had a long career in Hindi cinema spanning over 300 films, was seen visibly emotional at the crematorium.

With Kohli's passing, the industry loses a filmmaker whose work helped launch careers that would define Bollywood for decades. The motorcycle-split scene remains his most enduring legacy — a single image that encapsulated the fearless, larger-than-life spirit of 1990s Hindi cinema.
